text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- Serbian parliament sets session for April 15. Agenda to include the bill on the 1996 final budget statement.
- The Serbian-Kosovo Albanian round table in New York resembles talks on changing Yugoslavia's internal map judging by statements of some Kosovo Albanian officials.
- Yugoslav airlines JAT plans to reopen its direct flight to Peking at the end of May.
- Businessmen criticise state for giving special treatment to public firms and insufficient support to exporters at meeting of the Serbian Chamber of Commerce board of directors.
NASA BORBA
- The EU will probably approve autonomous trade measures to Yugoslavia at its April 29 ministerial council meeting in Luxembourg.
- Private bank Karic Banka dismissed 50 part-time employees last week and is planning to dismiss 100 full time workers while some experts have left of their own free will, paper sources say.
- Croatian Serbs say they will take part in the upcoming local elections provided population who lived there in 1991 is allowed to take part.
- Yugoslav Crown Prince Aleksandar Karadjordjevic says his alleged critical letter to Serbian Patriarch Pavle is a forgery and the Patriarch acknowledges he never received such a letter.
- Ten Belgrade secondary schools to hold one-day warning strike over unpaid wages.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Reconstruction of Belgrade-Bar railroad uncertain due to lack of funds. Around 92 million dinars needed for the works.

- Some 1,000 Yugoslavs believed to have been engaged in the civil war in Zaire, of whom 100 are former members of the Yugoslav airforce. Eight planes formerly belonging to the Yugoslav army flew to Zaire.
BLIC
- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic says she did not sign decree on Yugoslav-Bosnian Serb special ties agreement nor did she authorise vice-president Dragoljub Mirjanic to do so.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Montenegro and Slovakia signed in Bratislava a $112 million joint venture agreement for construction of a coastal water pipeline.

- "I believe that consequences created by the statements of some government members are not of such a nature as to call for their replacement," wrote Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic in a letter to president Momir Bulatovic.

- Executive board of the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists said the letter sent by Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic to President Momir Bulatovic is a step back on the last government press release of march 27, particularly concerning the role of the DPS in creation of state policy.

- The current government of Montenegro should be supported and not destabilised, said Montenegrin Parliament Speaker Svetozar Marovic in his public address Tuesday requesting a halt to divisions in the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists.
- Montenegrin Information Ministry condemned the media campaign against Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.
- International furniture fair was opened in Budva Tuesday.
- Libel trial of editor-in-chief of the Liberal Alliance party paper Liberal postponed to May 8.
- We will know tomorrow if metals factory Radoje Dakic will get money and restart production after 15 days of strike, said the company's general manager Zoran Popovic.
